r3_note: Many disputed rows were questions during the drill (is it X or Y?) - dropped per the reader brief. D4/D5 are the masc/fem adjective after مرة: one voiced (D4), one let pass (D5). D14 folded into D15. A2's t_amal (06:10) comes before his line (06:43); the transcript order is odd there, timing only.

rows.medi_said: أنا أملوهن هلأ. أنا أمل-- أملهم هلأ.
rows.amal_said: عملتهم.
rows.why: Asked عملتهم؟ he answered with a broken past form (amalhon / amalhom) for 'I did them'; she recast عملتهم and he said Yes.

rows.medi_said: ست أيام أسبوع ولا أسبوع؟ (I don't know how to say per.)
rows.amal_said: بالاسبوع.
rows.why: He said he did not know how to say 'per' and left أسبوع bare; Amal supplied بالاسبوع (her line is stamped 06:10, out of order in the transcript).

rows.medi_said: أنا أخذت وقت إضافه لـ قهوة
rows.amal_said: وقت زيادة يمن؟ ... إضافة ... it's فصحى. We say زيادة in spoken.
rows.why: He used MSA إضافة for 'extra'; Amal recast وقت زيادة and said إضافة is Fusha, spoken is زيادة (sheet: extra / increase | Ziaadeh | زيادة).
rows.english: I took extra time for coffee.

rows.amal_said: No. What's the other way to say it? ... أول مرة إلي ... The عندي rule is just with مفضل.
rows.why: For 'my first time' he used عندي; Amal said No and taught أول مرة إلي - عندي only goes with مفضل (Latin in transcript).

rows.amal_said: المرة الأولى إلي.
rows.why: مرة is feminine so the adjective after it is el-oola; he said el awwal at 18:43, 19:04 and 20:54, Amal recast المرة الأولى إلي at 20:58 and he said 'El mara el ula ... you didn't correct me on the other one'.
rows.r3_why: Real and separate from A4 (andi -> إلي): a different wrong piece. One row at the first try (18:43); her recast at 20:58 fixed it and he took it.

rows.medi_said: so aglab el marra is most of the time.
rows.amal_said: Yeah, but we don't say that. So أغلب الوقت.
rows.why: 'Most of the time' is أغلب الوقت; مرة is an occurrence, Amal said 'we don't say that' and gave الوقت.

rows.amal_said: No. ... Or maybe the it is feminine.
rows.why: 'The beginning of it' is awal + pronoun ending (awalo/awalha); he put min; Amal said No and he got to awala/awalaha.

rows.amal_said: No, kees is a plastic bag. ... Remember suitcase. ... Shanta.
rows.why: For 'bag' he tried كيس (plastic bag) then جزدان; Amal said No, kees is a plastic bag, and led him to شنتة (sheet: bag | Shanta | شنتة).

rows.amal_said: Does that sound right? ... Akhir shantata means like the end of her bag. ... That's the end of her bag.
rows.why: 'Her last bag' with آخر + el- / possessive means 'the end of (her) bag'; Amal prompted twice and he reached شنتة الـ أخيرة (Great job).

rows.amal_said: No.
rows.why: He put آخر after the noun with a pronoun ending; after the noun the adjective form a5eera is needed; Amal said No.

rows.amal_said: No. ... Just one way to say this thing.
rows.why: 'The end of our program' is آخر + noun with the pronoun ending (آخر برنامجنا), no el- and no لنا; Amal said No.

rows.amal_said: That's her last program. No. How do you say the end of?
rows.why: He used the adjective (and a plural أخرين) after the noun, which means 'her last program', not 'the end of'; Amal said No and he got آخر برنامجها.

rows.amal_said: No. ... It means the beginning of their cat.
rows.why: 'Their first cat' with أول + a possessed noun means 'the beginning of their cat'; Amal said No (engine wrote بسيطًا for bsset-hom).

rows.amal_said: Their.
rows.why: He put -na (our) on cat; Amal said 'Their.' to fix the owner ending (engine wrote بسطنا).

rows.amal_said: No.
rows.why: The 'other way' for 'her second cup' is taani before the noun + إلها; he put the possessed noun first then ثانية لها; Amal said No, then Great for ثانية كاسا لها.

rows.amal_said: جواب is one. أجوبة.
rows.why: He guessed a plural Ajwab for 'answers'; Amal gave the plural أجوبة.

rows.amal_said: No. ... It's tied to غير. ... عن، عن.
rows.why: 'Other than / different from' is غير عن; he used min; Amal said No and gave عن (she says he keeps forgetting it).

rows.medi_said: راح. This will be راح يكون الـأخر-- ... أخر مرة
rows.amal_said: Only one correction is مرة، مرة is feminine or masculine. So راح شو؟
rows.why: ykoon must match feminine مرة; Amal named the gender of مرة and he said راح تكون.
rows.english: It will be the last time.
rows.r3_why: Both readers agree on the slip; B9 (person on ykoon) is the exact rule - ykoon matching its subject.

rows.amal_said: آخر مرة بعملها.
rows.why: A plain present verb needs b-; he said أملها, Amal recast بعملها and repeated it.
rows.english: The last time I do it.

rows.amal_said: You are bad. ... You don't need منكون، خلص، بس سيئين.
rows.why: No 'to be' in the plain present; Amal said 'You don't need منكون'.

rows.amal_said: You don't need منكون، خلص، بس سيئين.
rows.why: 'We two' needs the plural adjective سيئين; he said singular سيء; Amal recast سيئين and he repeated it.

rows.amal_said: You don't need منكون، خلص، بس سيئين.
rows.why: 'Bad at choosing' needs bi + the noun (بالاختيار); he put the bare verb بنختار after the adjective and she let that part pass (she fixed نكون and سيء, A18/A19).
rows.english: We are both bad at choosing.
rows.r3_why: Different piece from A18/A19; she did not touch بنختار, so grammar-B, low.

rows.amal_said: ما عنا.
rows.why: عند takes ma, not mish; Amal said ما عنا twice.

rows.medi_said: Can I say تنين now both of us?
rows.amal_said: إحنا الاثنين.
rows.why: He had used bare تنين for 'both of us' and then asked; Amal supplied إحنا الاثنين.

rows.amal_said: راح. ... نبي ندفع.
rows.why: ra7 takes a bare verb; Amal repeated راح as a prompt, then said ندفع and he said 'إحنا راح نطفا كتير' (engine wrote بنفتح / بنطفأ for bnedfa3).
rows.english: But we're going to pay a lot.

rows.medi_said: و إذا بنـ-- إذا بنـ-- نطفا كتير بدنا إشي ممتاز و special.
rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. What's special?
rows.why: iza keeps the b- (إذا بندفع); he started بنـ twice then dropped it to نطفا and she did not fix the verb.
rows.english: If we pay a lot we want something excellent and special.

rows.amal_said: What's special? You know it. ... مميز.
rows.why: English 'special' in an Arabic sentence; on her sheet: special | Mumayyaz | مميز; Amal asked for it and supplied مميز.
rows.english: We want something excellent and special.

rows.medi_said: راح نكون متأخرين ... متأخرين أول طيارة.
rows.amal_said: متأخرين على أول تيار.
rows.why: متأخر takes على; he left it out; Amal recast متأخرين على أول طيارة and he echoed 'متأخرين على؟'.
rows.english: We'll be late for the first flight.

rows.medi_said: would it be اسباني إلي or اسباني أني؟
rows.amal_said: لا، I say إسباني، إسباني تبعي.
rows.why: He asked how to say 'my Spanish'; Amal supplied إسباني تبعي.

rows.amal_said: شهر.
rows.why: Month is شهر (sheet: month | shahar | شهر); he said شهرة twice and Amal recast شهر.

rows.medi_said: So، شهر الماضي ما استعملت اسباني كتير.
rows.amal_said: mm-hmm.
rows.why: Right after her الشهر الماضي he dropped the first el-; noun + adjective needs el- on both; she let it pass.
rows.english: Last month I didn't use Spanish much.

held_one_reader.why: 'Let's see if I did them right' needs iza; she stopped him and asked 'إنه or إذا?', pointing at the linker.
held_one_reader.english: Now let's see if I did them right.
held_one_reader.r3_why: Her 'إنه، or إذا؟' right after his line is a voiced prompt on the linker; 'see if' takes iza.

held_one_reader.medi_said: um, would I say صح or مزبوط؟ ... مزبوط. Yeah, right?
held_one_reader.why: He asked which word for 'right' and leaned to مزبوط; Amal said صح is better.
held_one_reader.r3_why: A which-word question she answered by picking صح: a didn't-know, tier 0.

held_one_reader.medi_said: I agree. I don't know how to say I agree.
held_one_reader.amal_said: We have, we have a saying-- مظبوط عادي، مظبوط.
held_one_reader.why: He said he did not know 'I agree'; her reply starts with مظبوط. Low: her line runs into the saying she then quotes.
held_one_reader.r3_why: He asked how to say it and she gave مظبوط; tier 0, low.

held_one_reader.amal_said: That's عمر. عمر، شو عمرك؟ قديش عمرك؟
held_one_reader.why: He heard her العمر (age/life) as أمر (command); she asked 'What's عمر?' and taught it.
held_one_reader.r3_why: Listening miss of her word, she taught it; mode listening.

held_one_reader.why: Describing today's clothes he used the bare form with no b- (بلبس, or the participle لابس); she let it pass. Engine may have dropped the b-.
held_one_reader.r3_why: Bare البس in a statement about today; low because the engine can drop b-.

held_one_reader.medi_said: and then el thani, el aw- el mara el thani, yeah, is also second time.
held_one_reader.why: After feminine مرة the adjective is el-tanye (and marra tanye at 23:04); Amal discussed the meaning and let the form pass - the same slip she then caught with الأولى.
held_one_reader.r3_why: Masculine adjective after feminine مرة, twice (22:22, 23:04); she never voiced a fix, so grammar-B, one row.

held_one_reader.medi_said: شنتة الـ آخر. Or آخر الشن-- no.
held_one_reader.why: Asked for the second way to say 'her last bag' (after he got شنتة الأخيرة) he tried شنتة الـ آخر; Amal said 'No end, but something else' and gave آخر شنطة إلها.
held_one_reader.r3_why: A new wrong attempt 1.5 min after A8/A9, after he had got الأخيرة right; her 'No end' is an explicit no.

held_one_reader.why: He knew it was 'our' (34:22 'the end of our schedule') but put -ha on برنامج; Amal recast برنامجنا and he repeated it.
held_one_reader.r3_why: A separate pronoun-ending slip from A11 (the aa5er structure); her 'بس برنامجنا' is a voiced recast.

held_one_reader.amal_said: Very close. What's questions? ... Mm-hmm. أسألتك.
held_one_reader.why: He had the word أسئلة (Amal: 'very close') but dropped the -t before the owner ending; she prompted 'What's questions?' and he said أسيليتك, she confirmed أسألتك.
held_one_reader.r3_why: Grammar A3, not vocab: 'very close' shows he had the plural; the missing piece is the feminine -t before -ak, which he added after her prompt.

held_one_reader.why: He put the -ik ending on عن and then a noun; after her 'then everyone' he said 'ghayr ann ikul' and she said Yes.
held_one_reader.r3_why: Her English prompt is a voiced signal (PG-22); he fixed it to عن الكل and she confirmed.

held_one_reader.why: 'I kept using a lot of Arabic words' needs the plural كلمات; she laughed and let it pass. Low: garbled line.
held_one_reader.english: (I kept using) a lot of Arabic words.
held_one_reader.r3_why: Singular كلمة with كتير for many words; low because the line is garbled.

held_one_reader.medi_said: قبل شهر، uh, ما، ما استعملت اسباني كتير.
held_one_reader.amal_said: Do, do you wanna say the last month؟ ... الشهر الماضي. ... قبل is for ago.
held_one_reader.why: قبل + number = ago; for 'last month' it is الشهر الماضي. Amal asked if he meant 'the last month', led him to الماضي and explained قبل is for ago.
held_one_reader.english: Last month I didn't use Spanish much.
held_one_reader.r3_why: Grammar E6, not vocab: he knows قبل; the slip is the ago-rule used where 'last' was meant, and Amal named it ('قبل is for ago').
